submission.causalMechanism: Corroborated code-path mechanism: `workspace.exec_bound` (tools.rs:631) calls `self.state.execution.bind_bound(request)` which is proven by the schema test (`workspace_exec_bound_binding_forces_contained_local`, tests.rs:254-256) to set `execution_profile = ContainedLocal` unconditionally with no caller override, and then dispatches through `run_task_proposal_with_inputs`. Every proposal path ultimately validates via `validate_run_proposal_structure` (engine.rs ~5012), and the `windows_native` branch (engine.rs 4914-4927) rejects any profile != TrustedLocal with the literal error `windows_native currently supports trusted_local only`, and also rejects any non-empty `steps` (`windows_native currently supports one command only`). Multiple independent anchors (MCP tool def, MCP schema test, Core validator literal, and three docs) all name the same causal boundary, so this is not a single-file coincidence.
submission.nextFalsifier: The smallest next physical falsifier that does NOT move byte/path authority into World or Agent arguments is: add a Core-level integration fixture that admits an existing-Runtime Job whose durable ExecutionPlan was produced with `executionProfile=contained_local` AND `executionTarget=windows_native`, and prove that exact replay (idempotent existing-Job lookup, which `docs/runtime.md:155/165` and `docs/compatibility.md:35` say is resolved before current policy/provider inspection) returns the existing committed Job without the `validate_run_proposal_structure` profile gate being re-applied. The falsifier result binary: if exact replay of a `contained_local`+`windows_native` plan returns the committed Job and dispatches the Windows launcher, then the causal boundary is precisely the new-admission profile gate (engine.rs 4914-4927); if replay itself fails/denies, then the boundary additionally lives in the plan-decoding/provider-commit path and the next falsifier must move to the `run_task_proposal_with_inputs` → provider-commit → `windows_native` launcher-selection chain rather than the admission validator. This is the smallest decisive experiment because it requires no schema, no Tool, no argument, and no authority change — only a real reconstructed-Runtime fixture that persists a cross-target plan and exercises the exact-replay-before-policy invariant that both docs and compatibility matrix already claim.
